assets.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup / stylized-concept.
Deliverable: a precise SIX-VIEW orthographic character turnaround design sheet for 3D sculpture modeling, landscape, highest available resolution. ONE immutable porcelain chess-piece sculpture, seen by six cameras, NOT six variant designs.
Layout: exactly 3 columns by 2 rows, equal panels, evenly spaced with clear separation. Top row: FRONT, BACK, LEFT. Bottom row: RIGHT, TOP, BOTTOM. Put those exact small neutral English labels beneath each view, outside the sculpture. Solid clean warm-white background, no scene, no floor, no cast shadows, no grid, no title, no additional objects.
Camera specifications: FRONT directly frontal 0 degrees; BACK directly rear 180 degrees; LEFT true 90-degree side; RIGHT true opposite 90-degree side; TOP directly overhead looking vertically down; BOTTOM directly underneath looking vertically up. All are orthographic with no perspective distortion. Do not substitute 3/4 views for any camera. TOP must show the crown/head top and genuinely foreshortened shoulders/body/pedestal footprint, NOT a standing frontal figure. BOTTOM must show the flat ivory underside of the solid pedestal, which occludes the statue above it, NOT a front figure or a second top view. Use the SAME orthographic pixels-per-unit scale across cameras; upright views equal height and same baseline. Top/bottom smaller because of projected footprint, do not enlarge to standing height. Complete object inside each panel with generous margins.
Rendering: match reference glossy hand-painted porcelain, ivory glaze, exact colors and restrained gold highlights. Neutral diffuse lighting with consistent exposure and roughness, subtle highlights sufficient to show sculpted folds. Never move any body part or accessory between views. Fixed head tilt, hands, costume folds, decoration placement and pedestal geometry. Patterns belong to fixed surface locations and rotate with the object; no stamping the same frontal pattern onto every side. Hidden surfaces must be conservative continuations, not redesigns.
Identity lock from attached image: RED KING, the porcelain blacksmith worker. Exactly the same face and black soft work cap with low brim, glossy vermilion V-neck shirt and elbow-length sleeves, broad plain textured brown leather apron with two brown shoulder straps, deep red trouser legs, shiny black low shoes, small simple ivory polygonal plinth. Bare ivory forearms. His anatomical RIGHT elbow is bent with the right forearm across the apron and right hand holding the upright gold hammer handle at mid-waist; LEFT arm descends at his anatomical left hip. Hammer is vertical in front of the legs, gold block-shaped head resting on the pedestal BETWEEN the shoes; this location must not swap or disappear. Head is turned slightly towards his anatomical right as in reference, and that fixed pose rotates with every camera. Preserve the apron curved asymmetric hem and textured surface. Back completion: red shirt and red trousers, the same two brown apron straps continue over shoulders to waist tie; apron does not become a long red cape or skirt. Same cap from back and sides. Gold hammer never migrates behind the back or to opposite hand. No crown, weapon, military uniform, extra gold motifs or chess king cross. Bottom is plain solid ivory underside, no inscription, no holes.
